🇲🇽🌎 TULUM'S JAGUAR PARK: ENTRY GOES FREE, PUBLIC LAND STAYS PUBLIC

Sheinbaum announced the Parque del Jaguar is dropping its entrance fee — beaches free for everyone, and just 80 pesos for Mexican visitors to the archaeological zone (free on Sundays), the same rate as 2018. Foreign tourists pay 265. It goes in the Diario Oficial under Plan Tulum Renace. The Maya coast isn't a gated resort for the few — it's national patrimony with public access built in.

🇲🇽🌎 SHEINBAUM WILL ATTEND THE WORLD CUP FINAL — ON HER OWN TERMS

She skipped the opening ceremony — "we don't need to rub shoulders at the top." But Sheinbaum will be at the MetLife final this Sunday after a personal invitation from Trump, standing alongside Canada's Carney as the three leaders of the World Cup's co-host nations. Mexico shows up as an equal partner, not a supplicant — declining the pageantry, present for the moment that counts.

🇲🇽🛢️ MEXICO HOLDS THE LINE ON FUEL — 24 PESOS GASOLINE, 27 DIESEL

While Washington lets the oil majors set the price at the pump, Sheinbaum just reaffirmed Mexico's cap: gasoline stays at 24 pesos a liter, diesel at 27. The state holds it there through IEPS fiscal stimulus, Pemex supply at competitive prices, and a pact with gas stations — roughly 80% now in compliance, with holdouts publicly named. Fuel treated as a public good, not a speculative asset.
📸 Mañanera del Pueblo — Tulum, Quintana Roo, 17 de julio de 2026

🇲🇽✊ "We are a humanist government with a feminist heart." — Mara Lezama, Governor of Quintana Roo, Mañanera, 17 July 2026 Social policy as the axis, a gender lens, and attention to the roots of inequality — not just its symptoms. The framing for a mañanera held, for the first time, from Tulum, Quintana Roo.

🇲🇽🎨 The Jaguar Park in Tulum will be free — and Mexicans pay a fraction to see their own heritage. — Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, 17 July 2026 Free entry to Parque del Jaguar. The archaeological zone: 80 pesos for Mexicans, 265 for foreigners. Electric transport, 20 pesos. The dividing wall comes down, replaced by a Maya-designed arch. The heritage belongs to the people, not to speculation.

🇲🇽🔍 Targets wanted by the US and Europe — captured on Mexican soil, under Mexican law. — Omar García Harfuch, Security Secretary, Mañanera, 17 July 2026 Priority targets requested by the United States and European countries were detained in Quintana Roo by Mexican forces. Oct 2024–June 2026: 3,794 arrests, 6,688 kg of drugs and 762 firearms seized. Cooperation, not subordination.

🇲🇽🔍 Quintana Roo: homicides down 85%. From nearly two killings a day in September 2024 to 0.3 in June 2026 — the lowest month in 12 years. — Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, 17 July 2026 Tulum: two straight months with zero homicides, and July still clean at report time. High-impact crime down 15% year over year. The result of the governor's work and the Security Cabinet's coordination.

🇲🇽✊ "Honesty, love for the people and the homeland — of course they deliver results." — Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, 17 July 2026 They said security couldn't improve without an iron fist or deals with the powerful. Quintana Roo just posted an 85% drop in homicides. Fighting corruption from the top down is the first security policy of the Fourth Transformation.
